title: Rav Huna bar Chalvan
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Shabbat 139b the Rabbis said to Rav Ashi: “Let the Master see this Torah scholar — Rav Huna bar Rabbi Chiyun is his name, and some say Rav Huna bar Rabbi Chalvan is his name — who took a clove of garlic,” etc.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The William Davidson digital Shabbat 139b paragraph fully writes Rav Huna ben Rabbi Chiyun, alternatively beRabbi Chalvan, restoring the father’s title omitted from the earlier translation. The Vilna Rashi digital comment defines ברא דתומא as צלע של שום, a clove of garlic, not garlic seed.

The checked Shabbat 139b paragraph fully writes Rav Huna ben Rabbi Chiyun, alternatively beRabbi Chalvan. Rashi’s complete comment defines ברא דתומא as a clove of garlic. These witnesses support the contextual titles and food term; they do not establish identity with another Huna or normalize the two patronymic forms.
